g_policy.reason: The offer copy states the 60-minute reward before an optional game. The decline and ad-failure fields leave normal access intact and address unavailable or unverified plays.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward field gives temporary priority routing, not cash or an externally exchangeable benefit.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is returning to the profile menu from the upgrade entry, not anything in a chat.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The adds field introduces a cap on how many characters free users can text. That limits a free activity, and a cap on distinct characters is not a cap on model replies or queue priority.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is a card in the s09 profile-menu drawer over the safe s08 profile screen, away from chats.

c1_revealed_value.reason: The reward is a time-limited slice of priority routing, which Janitor+ offers according to s02.e06.

c2_evidence.reason: s09.e31 supports the upgrade-menu entry, and s02.e06 supports the paid faster-replies benefit. The daily character limit is described as a proposed addition, not an existing app limit.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The offered to and subscribers fields specify that only free users see the card.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward expires after 60 minutes, while s02.e06 identifies priority routing as a paid benefit.

c5_moment.reason: The trigger occurs after the user returns to the persistent s09 profile menu; the card does not interrupt an ongoing chat.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The flow uses a sponsored game triggered by a detectable menu-return event, and the ad-failure field says unverified play does not turn on faster replies.

c7_specific.reason: The idea ties the s09 Upgrade to Janitor Plus entry to the priority-routing benefit shown at s02.e06.

other_concern: The claim that temporary priority routing is cheap to provide is not established by the product model.
